documentcloud_description: All records relating to a study on radioactivity levels in northern Canada that involved autopsies of Indigenous persons, specifically those conducted at the Charles Camsell Hospital (CCH) in Edmonton. All records contained within the file titled "Radioactive Fallout Study in Northern Canada," with the reference number RG29, Volume 2886, File 851-1-27, and date range 1963-1966. All memoranda, letters, and correspondence between the Department of National Health & Welfare’s Medical Services and regional superintendents from 1952-1964 concerning “Radioactivity Level in Northern Canada” or “autopsies performed on Eskimos and Indians”. Any reports, data analyses, or studies on the effects of atmospheric nuclear weapons testing, particularly those that caused radioactive fallout in the Canadian Arctic, on Indigenous communities and civilian populations during the period of 1952-1964. All records from the Radiation Protection Division that mention these studies or the health effects of nuclear fallout, including the "long range study" related to Strontium-90 and Cesium-137. Records describing the collection, preservation, shipment, and analysis of biological samples, including bones and teeth, from the aforementioned autopsies. All documents detailing the role of the Charles Camsell Hospital and its staff in these investigations. All records concerning government advisories or policies on the consumption of caribou meat and other Indigenous food sources that may have been affected by radioactive fallout.

documentcloud_description: Pursuant to the Access to Information Act, I am requesting records related to any employee tracking software used at the Case Processing Centre - Mississauga (CPC-M) of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC). Specifically, I am seeking information regarding the deployment, functionality, and usage of any software used to monitor employees' computer activity, including but not limited to tracking login and logout times. Scope of Request: I am requesting access to records, reports, policies, internal communications, technical documentation, and any other relevant information concerning: Software Name & Purpose: The name(s) of any employee tracking software used at CPC-M. The purpose of implementing this software. The department or authority responsible for overseeing its use. Employee Activity Tracking: Details on what employee activities are monitored, including: Login and logout timestamps. Duration of active computer use. Idle time or inactivity tracking. Website browsing history or internet usage monitoring. Applications or software used during work hours. Keystroke logging or mouse activity tracking, if applicable. Email and internal messaging monitoring, if applicable. File access, modification, or transfer tracking. Data Collection & Retention: The type of data collected from employees. How long the collected data is stored. Policies on data retention and deletion. Security measures in place to protect collected employee data. Employee Awareness & Consent: Policies or procedures informing employees about the software's use. Whether employees have provided consent for tracking. Any training materials, guidelines, or notices distributed to staff. Access & Use of Collected Data: Who has access to the collected data (e.g., supervisors, IT staff, HR, management). How the data is used for performance evaluation, attendance tracking, or other purposes. Whether the data has been used in employee disciplinary actions. If any audits or reviews of the software's use have been conducted. Legal & Compliance Considerations: Compliance with federal privacy laws, including the Privacy Act and related Treasury Board directives. Any privacy impact assessments conducted prior to software deployment. Any complaints, concerns, or investigations related to the use of this software. Technical Documentation & Contracts: Any agreements or contracts with third-party vendors providing the software. Technical specifications or manuals for the software. Records of system updates or modifications to the tracking capabilities. I request that these records cover the period from January 01, 2022 to February 28, 2025. If any records are exempt from disclosure, I request that non-exempt portions be provided, as per Section 25 of the Access to Information Act. Additionally, if the information exists in electronic format, I prefer to receive it in that format. Only provide the final copy or the latest draft of a document. Only provide you with the final email in a chain of emails.

documentcloud_description: I am seeking detailed information regarding all non-governmental organizations (NGOs) that receive funding from Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), specifically those engaged in activities aimed at combating racism and discrimination. This includes, but is not limited to, Kelowna Community Resources, Central Okanagan Local Immigration Partnership (COLIP), and The United Against Discrimination (UAD) Coalition, formerly known as the Organize Against Racism and Hate (OARH). Given recent troubling events in Kelowna involving the Sikh community, including physical and institutional attacks, it is crucial to understand the effectiveness and scope of actions taken by these funded organizations. We have had complaints that local organizations are not doing enough to help the Sikh community, which has faced multiple hate crimes. For instance, the tragic death of Harmandeep Kaur, the attack on Gagandeep Singh, and the systemic issues faced by Dr. Hoonjan are indicative of a broader problem that requires immediate attention. Therefore, I am requesting: Detailed Reports and Evaluations: Information on the specific activities undertaken by these NGOs to combat discrimination against the Sikh community in Kelowna. This should include strategies, program implementations, and outcomes related to tracking and responding to hate crimes. Funding Details: Documents detailing the amounts and conditions of funding provided to these NGOs by IRCC, including any specific requirements related to addressing hate crimes against Sikhs. Redaction of Sensitive Information: While I understand the sensitivity of the information, I request that all personal details such as names, addresses, or other identifiers be redacted to protect individual privacy. The focus of this request is on organizational actions and government oversight, not on individuals per se. Compliance and Accountability Reports: Any available compliance reports or assessments that evaluate the efficacy of funded programs in achieving their anti-discrimination goals.

documentcloud_description: Applications to Canada, under all streams, have questions to determine admissibility. Such as "have you ever been refused a visa or permit, denied entry or order to leave Canada or any other country or territory" amongst other similar questions. There is LOTS of litigation around files that were refused, with many applicants being cited for misrepresentation, even though the typical argument would have been "I didn't understand the question" or "I didn't realize this included all countries in the world". There have been many requests to make these questions simpler and less convoluted. For some reason IRCC has never felt the need to make these questions clearer. One suspects it just acts as an easy way to refuse a file. It's very likely that IRCC has sought numerous legal opinions over the years, whether these opinions are sough internally or externally. I want to see all instances of such opinions, including any and all correspondence related to this issue, including any discussions or meetings or reports or papers or presentations. Ensure to include any and all third party requests related to this, and any response/s given. From 2020-01-01 to 2025-07-09. Remove duplicate copies of documents and emails. Mark all Cabinet Confidences as non-relevant.

documentcloud_description:
I am requesting access to all records, including but not limited to internal and external emails, memoranda, briefing notes, meeting minutes, correspondence, presentations, policy papers, internal reports, consultation summaries, stakeholder feedback, and working documents, held by the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC), related to Halal mortgages (also known as Shariah-compliant home financing). 
The time frame for this request is December 24, 2024 to the present [July 5, 2025]. 

Specifically, this request includes any records that reference or relate to: 
Whether CMHC or the Government of Canada has considered, planned, or decided to offer mortgage default insurance for Halal mortgages, and if so, any details or timelines of such plans. 
All internal or interdepartmental rationale or reasoning for either supporting or not supporting Halal mortgage insurance. 
CMHC’s estimation of market demand for Halal mortgages in Canada, including any data, forecasts, or research conducted or commissioned on this topic. 
CMHC’s analysis or opinion regarding whether CMHC should support Halal mortgages from a policy, regulatory, financial risk, or equity perspective. 
Feedback received by CMHC from any stakeholders—including lenders, mortgage brokers, community organizations, and religious institutions—regarding Halal mortgages. 
Any discussions, communications, or documentation involving Budget 2024 commitments or follow-up consultations between CMHC and: 
Department of Finance Canada Department of Housing, Infrastructure and Communities. Any financial sector representatives Muslim community stakeholders regarding the accessibility or support of Halal mortgages. 

If any records are held in draft form, or marked as "not for distribution," I still request access to those versions under section 4 of the Access to Information Act. Thank you

All records created between July 1, 2025 (the approximate discovery date) and October 31, 2025, related to the interstellar object known as "3I/ATLAS" (also designated C/2025 N1). 
To assist in your search, this request includes, but is not limited to, the following types of records: 
1. High-Level Briefings and Assessments: All Briefing Notes, Memoranda to the Minister (MNs), or Advice to the Minister regarding 3I/ATLAS. All Briefing Notes or Memoranda to the Deputy Minister (DM) regarding 3I/ATLAS. All presentation decks (e.g., PowerPoint files) created for senior management (Director General level and above) describing the object's nature, characteristics, observed anomalies (e.g., non-gravitational acceleration, unusual composition), or trajectory. 
2. Internal and External Communications: All internal emails, memos, meeting agendas, and minutes where the "nature," "origin," "composition," "anomalies," "technosignatures," or "non-natural origin" of 3I/ATLAS are discussed. All communications and briefings received by the department from any other government department (OGD) (e.g., DND, NRC, PCO, ISED) or external partner (e.g., NASA, ESA, NORAD, Five Eyes (FVEY) partners, the 'Sky Canada Project' team, or university-affiliated astronomers) regarding 3I/ATLAS. 
3. Scientific and Security Assessments: All scientific or technical analyses, reports, or data summaries created or received by the department regarding 3I/ATLAS's properties (e.g., spectral analysis, composition, radio signals, light curve). The vast majority of large public bodies use a records and data management system to track and manage Freedom of Information (FOI) requests. We are seeking access to the following fields:
1. Identifier: The request number or unique identifier for each request.
2. Summary: The most detailed request text available in the tracking system, be that the full request text or a summary written by a FOI coordinator.
3. Date received: The date each FOI was received.
4. Date completed: The date each FOI was completed.
5. Disposition: The disposition for each FOI (records granted in full, in part, denied, etc.).
6. (Not mandatory) Department, division, body or entity: If your tracking system provides details on which part of your organization is being targeted with a request, we would like this information.

We are seeking the above information for FOIs that were completed between July 1, 2024, and March 31, 2026. 

We are only seeking access to data from general records requests, not personal records requests. We are not seeking access to information about FOIs that are not yet completed, or FOIs that were withdrawn, abandoned or transferred to another institution. In rare instances, institutions are consulted on FOIs received by other institutions, and this interaction is captured in their tracking systems. We are not interested in requests that your organization does not have custody of. If you cannot easily filter out these unwanted requests—incomplete, withdrawn, abandoned, transferred, consultations—that's fine. Send us what you have. You do not need to check with us about this.

We require this data in a machine-readable table format (Excel or CSV, for instance).

documentcloud_description:
Please provide a record or records (if they exist) that describe the following:
• For the 43rd and 44th general elections, the processing of special ballots, including how, where and by whom they were counted (if different from the 45th general election)
• For the 43rd, 44th and 45th general elections, the processing and counting of ballots for advance polls, including the transportation of ballot boxes from advance polls to counting locations
• For 43rd, 44th and 45th general elections, the processing of vote-by-mail ballots, including who processes vote-by-mail ballot requests, and the criteria to accept or reject requests to vote by mail
• Reports for the 2019, 2021 and 2025 federal elections about instances of voters being told at the polls that they had already voted by mail-in ballot when they had not
• The process for Elections Canada workers to report such issues
• The definitions, according to Elections Canada, of the following terms: voting kit, special ballot and vote by mail, including any changes to these definitions during the 2019, 2021 and 2025 federal elections.

Or, if there have been explicit directives, meetings, documents, and the like around guiding clinical practitioners to not find someone ineligible because they have undergone clinical, transition-related care. I am unsure who holds this information, but this has come up in discussions with doctors providing clinical exams to transgender migrants as something that has been of discussion within the IRCC. Seeking Briefing notes (including annexes), Discussions/Opinions/Position Papers, Emails (including attachments), Ministerial announcements or news items, Manuals, Policies and directives, Reports, Presentation materials, and Standard Operating Procedures. Requesting records and statistical data related to federal offenders under community supervision in Ontario during the period January 1, 2023, to present.

2. Related Internal Reports Any Death in Custody reports, Board of Investigation (BOI) reports, or internal summaries regarding the deaths of federal parolees in Ontario during this timeframe. 

3. Revocation & Re-Incarceration Data - The number of federal parolees in Ontario who were revoked and re-incarcerated within 90 days of release, broken down by supervision type and year. 

4. Supervision & Oversight Challenges - Any internal memos, audits, policy reviews, or reports from CSC, the Parole Board of Canada, or regional parole offices in Ontario concerning: Parolee deaths in the community Failures or gaps in risk assessment Community resource constraints impacting supervision Caseload pressures and staffing shortages.

5. Demographics of Deceased Parolees (Anonymized) Breakdown by: Age group Gender Race/ethnic group (if available in aggregate format) Mental health status or known diagnosis (if available) Addiction or substance use history (where tracked).

6. Parole Supervision Conditions & Compliance Number of parolees in Ontario with Section 133 special conditions (e.g., residency, curfew, no-contact, substance abstention), by year and release type Data on breaches or violations of special conditions prior to revocation or death. 

7. Caseload Data Average number of parolees per parole officer in Ontario, broken down by year (2023 - 2025 YTD), by district or region. 

8. Police Collaboration - Any Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs), policies, or internal guidance related to collaboration with municipal or provincial police regarding: Deaths of parolees in the community Information sharing after parole breaches, overdoses, or reoffending.

documentcloud_title: 2026-07 - CLC-A-2024-004 - Canada Lands Company CLC Limited
documentcloud_description: This access to information request aims to obtain copies of all documents and information held by Canada Lands Company regarding the pumping station for sanitary and storm sewers located on lots 3 086 741and 3 086 851 of the Quebec cadastre (hereinafter the "Lots") owned by it in the Saint Hubert borough of the City of Longueil. Specifically, we are making this access to information and documents request to obtain copies of all documents and information held by Canada Lands Company regarding the pumping station for sanitary and storm sewers located on the lots, as well as all relevant information related to the sanitary and/or storm sewer service serving the lots and buildings in the southwest sector of the Saint-Hubert airport, including the buildings located at 4801, rue Leckie and 4801-3, rue Leckie. Without limitation, we wish to obtain all documents related to the pumping station for sanitary and storm sewers located on the Lots and held by Canada Lands Company, for example: Any authorization issued to Canada Lands Company (permits, ministerial authorization, etc.) regarding the construction, installation, and connection of the pumping station located on the Lots (including all documents that are an integral part of and listed in these authorizations); Any request for authorization or permit related to the connection of the pumping station located on the Lots submitted to MELCCFP by Canada Lands Company; Any authorization or permit related to the connection of the pumping station located on the Lots held by Canada Lands Company; Any request for authorization or permit related to the connection to the sanitary and/or storm sewer submitted to MELCCFP for the Lots by Canada Lands Company; Any authorization or permit related to the connection to the sanitary and/or storm sewer issued for the Lots to Canada Lands Company; Any inspection report produced by Canada Lands Company regarding the pumping station located on the Lots; Any notice of non-compliance or any other document regarding the pumping station located on the Lots; Any document regarding the sanitary and/or storm sewer services serving the Lots and buildings located at 4801, rue Leckie and 1111-3, rue Leckie; Any information related to the number and identification of properties served by the pumping station located on the Lots; Any other document held by Canada Lands Company regarding the ownership of the pumping station located on the Lots. Finally, please note that if this includes colour documents (plans, photos), we would like to have colour copies. All documents can be sent to us by email. For any additional information, please do not hesitate to contact the undersigned. We thank you for your attention to this request.

The total budget that has been allocated for ESDC’s Benefits Delivery Modernization program since January 2023 to October 2024, and an inventory of publicly visible releases since that time.   
A yearly total amount is one for "Total budget". (eg, 2022-2023: 301.4 million, etc.) A release could mean a new product or service, a new feature in an existing product or service, a significant improvement to an existing feature (eg, waiting time for X reduced by 90%), or public information about new services.   
An announcement of a future program/service/feature would not qualify as a release by this definition. Information on a release would likely be included in include any final reports and documents that accompany public deliverables (service improvements) from January 1st, 2023, to October 2024. 
In terms of the release (public service improvements) side of things, any new products/features/launches from the BDM program transmittal slips or status updates on the BDM program that include summaries of new services being launched or improvements to existing systems, that might of been captured in briefing notes to senior leaders that accompany SA&As or status updates created by BDM staff for presentations to senior leadership and BDM/TBS governance committees. The minister's LinkedIn announcement on "service delivery initiatives and improvements" which mentions "transforming benefits delivery technology" but does not specify exactly what has been released in this regard.

documentcloud_title: 2026-07 - A-2025-07391 - Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
documentcloud_description: I am writing to request clarification regarding the eligibility criteria under the Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSWP) for candidates currently residing and working inside Canada. Specifically, I would like to understand how the following scenarios are assessed for eligibility and CRS (Comprehensive Ranking System) points under Express Entry: A candidate is currently working full-time in Canada for a Canadian employer on a valid work permit. The same candidate is also working full-time remotely for a foreign company (outside Canada), in a capacity that aligns with a skilled occupation under the NOC system. I seek clarification on: Whether the work experience gained with the foreign employer while physically present in Canada can be considered valid foreign work experience under FSWP. Whether the Canadian work experience gained simultaneously is counted as eligible Canadian work experience under CEC or FSWP. If both experiences (Canadian and foreign) are recognized concurrently and how they impact the CRS calculation and eligibility under Express Entry. I respectfully request access to any internal documents, policy interpretation notes, or officer guidelines that address the evaluation of such scenarios for Express Entry eligibility and CRS scoring. Only provide the final copy or the latest draft of a document. Only provide the final email in a chain of emails. (From 2020-01-01 to 2025-04-01).

documentcloud_description: All records, including but not limited to internal memoranda, policy guidance, operational bulletins, briefing notes (including annexes), training materials, program delivery instruction supplements, system design or business rules documentation, standard operating procedures, manuals, and internal correspondence (including emails and attachments), that relate to the assessment and awarding of Additional Points for Canadian Education (15 or 30 points under Express Entry additional factors) in the Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) where a program of study, rather than the institution as a whole, is not eligible for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) at the time of electronic Application for Permanent Residence (e-APR), regardless of the institution's status as a designated learning institution (DLI) or the fact that the institution offers other PGWP-eligible programs, since PGWP eligibility also depends on the field of study. For clarity, this request concerns additional factors points for Canadian education only and does not seek records related solely to core human capital education points. This request includes records that address any of the following: 1. Instructions, guidance, or training provided to officers on how to assess, retain, or remove additional CRS points for Canadian education when the Express Entry system awards such points at the profile stage, but the program of study is determined to be not eligible for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) at the time of electronic Application for Permanent Residence (e-APR), including any records that interpret or operationalize the guidance that institutions or programs not eligible for a PGWP at the time of e-APR should not be awarded CRS points for additional factors. 2. Internal clarification or interpretation of Program Delivery Instructions stating that programs of study not eligible for a PGWP at the time of e-APR should not be awarded additional CRS points for Canadian education, and how this requirement is applied during application assessment. 3. Documentation describing the business rules, known limitations, or identified gaps of the Express Entry profile builder in distinguishing between: a. PGWP eligibility of a program of study during the period of study, and b. PGWP eligibility of a program of study at the time of e-APR submission, for the purpose of awarding additional CRS points for Canadian education. 4. Internal communications between policy, program delivery, and systems or digital teams that discuss alignment or discrepancies between Express Entry system logic and officer-facing guidance relating specifically to program-level PGWP eligibility, including field-of-study requirements, and the awarding of additional CRS points for Canadian education. Time frame for this request is: June 1, 2024, to the February 12, 2026. Exclusions: This request does not seek case-specific records, individual applicant files, or personal information. Remove duplicate copies of documents and emails. Remove any records or parts of records that are not related to the subject of the request.
